# Boss appears in both lists on index screen

> **Producer clarification (2026-09-21, audit rejection) — supersedes the original direction below.**
> "There are still two bosses, one appears in the left menu the other in the right.
> They should both be in the right. In addition the one currently in the right should be renamed to Boss."
>
> Resolved direction: the boss appears **exactly once**, in the **ENEMIES list (right column)**
> with the label **"Boss"**. The `GymBoss` entry must be **removed from the scene list (left column)**.
> The original "Problem statement"/"Desired change" text below described the opposite placement and
> is retained only as historical context.

## Problem statement

The Boss entry appears in both columns of the gym index screen: as `GymBoss` in the scene list (left column) and as `Boss` in the enemy entries list (right column). It should only appear once — in the scene list as the dedicated `GymBoss` combat scene.

## Users

- **Developer / player** browsing the gym index — expects one entry per distinct gym scene, no duplicates.

### Example user stories

- As a **developer**, I want the Boss to appear only once on the gym index (as `GymBoss`) so I don't see a confusing duplicate entry.
- As a **developer**, I want the enemy entries list to only show archetypes that don't already have a dedicated gym scene.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Boss only in ENEMIES list (right column) [revised per producer clarification]:** The `GymIndex` right "ENEMIES" column includes a "Boss" entry (enemyKey `boss`), and the left scene column does NOT include `GymBoss` / "Boss".
- [ ] **AC2 — Other enemies unaffected:** All other enemy entries (scout, diver, tank, phaser, swarm, asteroid) remain in the ENEMIES list unchanged.
- [ ] **AC3 — Tests pass:** All existing tests updated and the full test suite passes.
- [ ] **AC4 — All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] **AC5 — Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Minimal change:** Only filter `boss` from the enemy entries in `GymIndex.ts`; do not modify `enemyGymDiscovery.ts` or `enemyConfig.ts`.
- **No behavioural change** to GymBoss or any other gym scene.

## Existing state

- `GymIndex.ts` creates two columns: `entries` (gym scenes from `discoverGymScenes`, filtered to exclude `GymEnemies`) and `enemyEntries` (enemy configs from `discoverEnemyGymEntries`, no filtering).
- `GymBoss` is a standalone gym scene (created in AH-0MT99QBDW001O7PE) and is the canonical boss combat scene.
- The `boss` key in `DEFAULT_ENEMY_CONFIGS` generates a duplicate entry in the enemy list.

## Desired change

> **Superseded:** the code shown here (filtering boss *out* of enemy entries) is the
> pre-clarification approach and was rejected. The implemented change is the inverse:
> filter `GymBoss` out of the scene list and keep `boss` in the enemy list.

In `GymIndex.ts`, filter out `boss` from `this.enemyEntries` after discovery — similar to how `GymEnemies` is already filtered from `this.entries`. A one-line change:

```ts
this.enemyEntries = this.enemyEntries.filter((e) => e.enemyKey !== 'boss');
```

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/GymIndex.ts` — Filter `GymBoss` from the scene list; keep `boss` in enemy entries.
- `src/scenes/GymIndex.test.ts` — Update test assertions: `boss` present in `listedEnemyScenes`, absent from `listedScenes`.

## Related work

- **Create Boss (Central AI) gym scene (AH-0MT99QBDW001O7PE)** — created the dedicated `GymBoss` scene that should be the sole boss entry.
- **Refactor Enemy Gym Scenes (AH-0MT985FOA008JWM9)** — related refactor that established the two-column index pattern.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk: Low.** The change is a single filter on an already-established list. No new code paths.
- **Assumption:** The boss enemy config is intentionally kept in `DEFAULT_ENEMY_CONFIGS` (for other uses like combat mode), only the index display needs filtering.

## Scope-creep note

- If the operator wants the enemy entries list to auto-filter ALL enemies that have dedicated gym scenes (not just boss), that should be a separate item — out of scope here.

# Power Ups scene title in index page

## Problem statement

The gym index derives each scene's display label by stripping the leading
`Gym` from the scene key (`src/utils/gymDiscovery.ts` → `displayLabelFromKey`).
`GymPowerUpsCombat` therefore reads **"PowerUpsCombat"**, but the threat-free
power-up gym `GymPowerUps` reads simply **"PowerUps"** — an ambiguous,
unclassified label next to its combat counterpart. Rename the scene so its
derived label becomes **"PowerUpsUtility"**.

## Users

- **Developer / play-tester** opening the dev gym index to pick a scene.
  - *As a developer, I want the threat-free power-up gym to be clearly labelled
    so I can distinguish it from the combat power-up gym at a glance.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Scene rename:** the non-combat power-up gym is renamed
  `GymPowerUps` → `GymPowerUpsUtility` across file, class and scene key:
  `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsUtility.ts`, `export class GymPowerUpsUtility`,
  `super({ key: 'GymPowerUpsUtility' })`. Its test file is renamed to match.
- [ ] **AC2 — Index label:** the gym index lists the scene with the label
  **"PowerUpsUtility"** (and still lists `PowerUpsCombat` unchanged), sorted
  alphabetically: `Boss, Player, PowerUpsCombat, PowerUpsUtility, Weapons`.
  Asserted in `src/scenes/GymIndex.test.ts`.
- [ ] **AC3 — No stale references:** no remaining occurrences of the bare
  identifier/key `GymPowerUps` (excluding `GymPowerUpsCombat`) in `src/`,
  `docs/`, or `README.md`.
- [ ] **AC4 — Behaviour unchanged:** spawning, lifecycle, collection, magnet,
  HUD and back-button behaviour of the scene are untouched (rename only); the
  scene-level test suite still passes.
- [ ] **AC5 — Documentation:** all related documentation is updated to reflect
  the changes, including code comments, `README.md`, and any relevant wiki or
  docs site entries (notably `docs/Game Design Document.md` and
  `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`).
- [ ] **AC6 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Rename only** — no functional/behavioural change to the scene.
- Follow the existing gym convention (`Gym<Name>.ts`, class and key `Gym<Name>`)
  so `import.meta.glob` auto-discovery and `sceneClassFromModule` continue to work.
- `GymPowerUpsCombat` must remain unchanged (label stays "PowerUpsCombat").
- Keep the index auto-discovery intact — do not hard-code labels in `GymIndex.ts`.

## Existing state

- `src/utils/gymDiscovery.ts` — `displayLabelFromKey()` strips a leading `Gym`;
  discovery is directory-driven via `import.meta.glob`.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUps.ts` — class `GymPowerUps`, key `'GymPowerUps'`.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUps.test.ts` — 37 references to the old name.
- `src/scenes/GymIndex.test.ts` — expects labels `['Boss','Player','PowerUps','PowerUpsCombat','Weapons']`
  and keys including `'GymPowerUps'`.
- Comment/doc references in `src/core/constants.ts`, `src/powerups/PowerUp.ts`,
  `src/ui/HUD.ts`, `README.md`, `docs/Game Design Document.md`,
  `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`.
- No runtime caller starts the scene by the literal key (the index auto-discovers it),
  so the rename is safe.

## Desired change

Rename the scene to `GymPowerUpsUtility` (file, class, scene key) and update the
matching test file plus all documentation/comment references. The gym index then
renders the label **"PowerUpsUtility"** via the existing derivation — no change to
`GymIndex.ts` or `gymDiscovery.ts` is required.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUps.ts` → `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsUtility.ts` — rename file, class and scene key
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUps.test.ts` → `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsUtility.test.ts` — rename file and update all references
- `src/scenes/GymIndex.test.ts` — update expected label (`PowerUpsUtility`) and key (`GymPowerUpsUtility`)
- `README.md` — rename the "GymPowerUps Gym Scene" section and path references
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — update the scene tree entry (key/label)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — update the scheme-aware routing reference
- `src/core/constants.ts`, `src/powerups/PowerUp.ts`, `src/ui/HUD.ts` — update code comments

## Related work

- **AH-0MUAYB2XR007N10W** – Player gym scene improvements (open) — sibling gym-index/label polish.
- **AH-0MTHG5JVP006U6K7** – Retire per-enemy gym scenes (completed) — prior gym-index restructuring.
- **AH-0MT7QQGBU008V4R0** – Write the Game Design Document (completed) — source of the scene-tree documentation.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the rename target is `GymPowerUpsUtility` (convention-consistent),
  producing label "PowerUpsUtility"; `GymPowerUpsCombat` is left untouched.
- **Risk:** a hard-coded `'GymPowerUps'` scene key would break at runtime — grep
  shows only tests, docs and comments reference it, so no runtime caller is affected.
- **Risk (low):** doc drift if any reference is missed — AC3 covers a repo-wide grep.
- **Scope-creep risk:** other gym scenes (e.g. "Weapons") may deserve clearer labels;
  record those as separate work items, not in this scope.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q:** What display label should the non-combat power-ups scene use in the gym index?
  (Options offered: "PowerUps (Basic)", "PowerUps (Simple)", "PowerUps (No Enemies)",
  "PowerUps (Threat-Free)".)
  — **Answer (producer, interactive reply):** "PowerUpsUtility — rename the GymPowerUps
  scene to achieve this." Source: work-item comment `AH-C0MUBU38ZM006722P` (recorded
  after producer reply). Related: AH-0MUAYB4EJ005CIYQ.
- **Q (agent assumption, not asked):** how is "PowerUpsUtility" realised given labels are
  auto-derived? — **Decision:** rename to `GymPowerUpsUtility` so `displayLabelFromKey`
  yields `PowerUpsUtility`, preserving the gym naming convention.
  Source: `src/utils/gymDiscovery.ts`, `docs/Game Design Document.md`.

# Test: Mineral entity lifecycle and collection semantics

## Summary

Test-first task pinning the `Mineral` collectable's contract **before** the
implementation child is built. These tests define the contract for parent AC1
of AH-0MUBVGI62004ED9Q: a mineral is a small gold dot that is collected on
overlap, is never hit by bullets, and causes no damage.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A test asserts a mineral spawns at a given position, renders as a small gold dot, and persists (no drift or despawn) until collected.
- A test asserts minerals are not hit by bullets and cause no damage or collision response on contact with the player or an enemy.
- A test asserts that flying the player ship into a mineral removes it and fires the collection callback exactly once.
- A test asserts that a non-asteroid enemy overlapping a mineral absorbs it (mineral removed, no damage).
- The new tests execute under `npm test`; they are expected to be red until the implementation child ("Mineral collectable entity and constants") lands, and the full suite passes once it does.

## Minimal implementation

1. Add a new unit test file for `Mineral` using the existing vitest setup.
2. Write the tests against the intended `Mineral` API; do **not** implement production code in this item.

## Key Files

- `src/entities/__tests__/Mineral.test.ts` (new)

## Dependencies

- None (first item in the plan).

## Deliverables

Definitive (initially red) tests pinning mineral lifecycle and collection semantics, consumed by the mineral entity implementation child.

# Test: Hold-full choice scene and PlayScene wiring

## Summary

Test-first verification task pinning the paused modal choice overlay and the
PlayScene mineral wiring (drop, collection, re-drop, overflow) **before** the
implementation child is built. Defines the contract for parent AC1/AC4/AC8 of
AH-0MUBVGI62004ED9Q.

## Acceptance Criteria

- When the mineral store reaches capacity, the game pauses and a modal overlay presents three distinct power-up options, pausing gameplay at the SceneManager level (mirroring `PauseScene`) so no further collection/damage occurs while choosing.
- Destroying a `small` asteroid spawns one or more mineral drops (small gold dots) at the destruction site; `large`/`medium` destructions do not themselves spawn minerals (their split children, once `small`, do). Minerals are not hit by bullets and cause no damage or collision response on contact with the player or an enemy.
- The hold-full choice resets the store to 0 carrying any overflow (store = collected − capacity) and resumes play.
- Tests assert re-drop on enemy death and player/enemy overlap collection are wired in PlayScene.
- The mechanic is covered by meaningful automated tests (mineral lifecycle/collection rules, enemy count + re-drop distribution bounds, hold overflow arithmetic, choice-strategy distinctness and permanence, scene wiring) with coverage reported; the full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Minimal implementation

1. Add scene-level tests for the mineral choice overlay (three options, SceneManager pause, selection resumes).
2. Add PlayScene integration tests for small-asteroid mineral spawn, overlap collection, enemy re-drop and store reset/overflow.
3. Write the tests against the intended API; do **not** implement production code in this item.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/__tests__/MineralChoiceScene.test.ts` (new)
- `src/scenes/__tests__/PlayScene.minerals.test.ts` (new)

## Dependencies

- Pluggable power-up choice strategy and permanent-effect support (the strategy the scene consumes).

Definitive (initially red) tests pinning the choice overlay and PlayScene wiring.

# Mineral collectable entity and constants

## Summary

Implement the `Mineral` collectable — a small, stationary gold dot that is
collected by overlap and is otherwise inert — plus its canonical constants.
This is the first end-to-end slice of AH-0MUBVGI62004ED9Q.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A new `Mineral` entity renders as a small gold dot at a spawn position, using new mineral visual/size/depth constants added to `src/core/constants.ts`.
- Minerals are not hit by bullets and cause no damage or collision response on contact with the player or an enemy.
- Flying the player ship into a mineral removes it and invokes a collection callback; a non-asteroid enemy overlapping a mineral absorbs it (mineral removed, no damage).
- Minerals are stationary and persist until collected (no drift, no lifetime despawn) unless a future tunable adds one.
- The tests from "Test: Mineral entity lifecycle and collection semantics" are green and the pre-existing suite still passes.

## Minimal implementation

1. Add mineral visual/size/depth constants to `src/core/constants.ts`.
2. Add `src/entities/Mineral.ts` with a spawn-at constructor and a player/enemy overlap handler that invokes a supplied collection callback.
3. Exclude the mineral from bullet collision groups and from any damage path.
4. Register the mineral with the scene's display/depth ordering consistent with existing drops.

## Key Files

- `src/entities/Mineral.ts` (new)
- `src/core/constants.ts` (modify)
- `src/entities/__tests__/Mineral.test.ts` (green)

## Dependencies

- Test: Mineral entity lifecycle and collection semantics (prerequisite).

## Deliverables

Working `Mineral` entity + constants, unit-tested.

# Mineral rules tunables and per-enemy mineral count

## Summary

Add the mineral tunables to the game-rules config and give non-asteroid
enemies per-enemy mineral accounting with a 25–50 % re-drop on death.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Collection amount (default 1), hold capacity (default 20), and the re-drop fraction range (default 25–50 %) are read from the game-rules config (`src/core/rules.ts`) with sensible defaults and corrupt-config fallback, matching the existing rules pattern.
- `BaseEnemy` tracks a per-enemy mineral count; every non-asteroid enemy that overlaps a mineral absorbs it (mineral removed, no damage) and increments that enemy's tracked mineral count; asteroids are excluded.
- When that enemy is destroyed, 25–50 % (configurable) of its collected count is re-spawned as individual mineral drops scattered at the explosion site, never exceeding the collected count.
- The tests from "Test: Enemy mineral count and re-drop distribution" are green and the pre-existing suite still passes.

## Minimal implementation

1. Extend the rules type + `loadRules()`/`saveRules()` defaults/merge in `src/core/rules.ts`.
2. Add mineral count state + `collectMineral()` to `src/entities/BaseEnemy.ts`.
3. Add a `mineralRedropCount(rng)` helper returning a value in the configured fraction range.
4. Spawn individual `Mineral` drops at the explosion site from the destruction path.

## Key Files

- `src/core/rules.ts` (modify)
- `src/entities/BaseEnemy.ts` (modify)
- `src/entities/__tests__/BaseEnemy.minerals.test.ts` (green)

## Dependencies

- Test: Enemy mineral count and re-drop distribution (prerequisite).

## Deliverables

Configurable mineral tunables + enemy accounting and re-drop, unit-tested.

# Ship's hold store, overflow arithmetic and HUD counter

Give the run a mineral store (ship's hold), expose it on the HUD, and handle
the overflow arithmetic that carries into the next hold.

- `GameState` gains a mineral store and capacity; flying the player ship into a mineral removes it and increases the ship's mineral store by the configured collection amount (default 1), up to the configured capacity (default 20).

- The tests from "Test: Ship's hold overflow and HUD counter" are green and the pre-existing suite still passes.

# Pluggable power-up choice strategy and permanent-effect support

## Summary

Introduce the pluggable selection strategy that supplies the three offered
power-ups, plus the mechanism that makes the chosen effect permanent for the run.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A new `src/powerups/choice.ts` defines a pluggable strategy interface; the default implementation is a random selection across the full existing drop pool (P3–P9 plus weapon drops), drawing distinct entries and degrading gracefully if the pool cannot supply three.
- Swapping the strategy requires no change to the choice scene or PlayScene wiring.
- Selecting one applies it to the player as a permanent effect for the current run (including weapon drops, which do not expire as they normally do).
- `src/powerups/effects.ts` and `src/entities/Player.ts` support marking a chosen effect permanent so it never expires for the run.
- The tests from "Test: Choice strategy distinctness and permanent effects" are green and the pre-existing suite still passes.

## Minimal implementation

1. Add `src/powerups/choice.ts` with the interface + default random-across-all-drops implementation.
2. Extend `EffectsRegistry` to mark an effect permanent (skip timer decrement).
3. Extend `Player` weapon equipping so a chosen weapon is permanent.
4. Keep the existing timed drop behaviour untouched for non-chosen drops.

## Key Files

- `src/powerups/choice.ts` (new)
- `src/powerups/effects.ts` (modify)
- `src/entities/Player.ts` (modify)
- `src/powerups/__tests__/choice.test.ts` (green)
- `src/powerups/__tests__/effects.permanent.test.ts` (green)

## Dependencies

- Test: Choice strategy distinctness and permanent effects (prerequisite).

## Deliverables

Pluggable choice strategy + run-permanent effect support, unit-tested.

# Choice modal scene and PlayScene mineral wiring

## Summary

Deliver the paused modal power-up choice overlay and wire the full mineral loop
into PlayScene: spawn on small-asteroid kill, collection, enemy re-drop, and
hold-full triggering.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A new `src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts` presents three distinct power-up options as a modal overlay that pauses gameplay at the SceneManager level (mirroring `PauseScene`) so no further collection/damage occurs while choosing.
- When the mineral store reaches capacity the game pauses and the overlay is presented; selecting one applies it to the player as a permanent effect for the current run, resumes play, and resets the store to 0 carrying any overflow (store = collected − capacity).
- Destroying a `small` asteroid spawns one or more mineral drops (small gold dots) at the destruction site; `large`/`medium` destructions do not themselves spawn minerals (their split children, once `small`, do).
- `PlayScene` wires player/enemy overlap collection and re-drop on enemy death at the explosion site.
- The tests from "Test: Hold-full choice scene and PlayScene wiring" are green and the pre-existing suite still passes.

## Minimal implementation

1. Add `src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts` mirroring `PauseScene` navigation/pause semantics.
2. In `PlayScene._onEnemyKilled`, spawn mineral(s) when `getSizeTier() === 'small'`.
3. Wire player/enemy overlap collection and enemy re-drop on destruction.
4. On hold-full, launch the choice scene, then apply the pick and reset the store with overflow.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts` (new)
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` (modify)
- `src/scenes/__tests__/MineralChoiceScene.test.ts` (green)
- `src/scenes/__tests__/PlayScene.minerals.test.ts` (green)

## Dependencies

Paused modal choice overlay + fully wired PlayScene mineral loop, integration-tested.

# Asteroids-only mineral gym, seeding and gym tests

## Summary

Add an asteroids-only gym scene that demonstrates the whole mineral mechanic in
isolation, register it in the gym index, and pre-seed existing gym scenes with
100 random mineral drops.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A new gym scene (asteroids only) is registered in the gym index and demonstrates: small-asteroid mineral drops, player hold fill, HUD counter, enemy collection, re-drop on enemy death, and the hold-full choice overlay.
- Existing gym scenes spawn 100 random mineral drops on initialisation.
- Gym tests cover the new scene launching from the index and the 100-drop seeding in existing gyms.
- The new gym tests are green and the pre-existing gym suite still passes.

## Minimal implementation

1. Add `src/scenes/gym/GymMinerals.ts` (asteroids-only) reusing `core/GymFormationScene`.
2. Seed 100 random minerals on init in the shared gym base / existing scenes.
3. Register the scene via the existing gym discovery/index convention.
4. Add gym tests for launch + seeding.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/gym/GymMinerals.ts` (new)
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` (modify)
- `src/utils/gymDiscovery.ts` / `src/scenes/GymIndex.ts` (register)
- gym test files (new/extended)

## Dependencies

- Choice modal scene and PlayScene mineral wiring (the mechanic the gym demonstrates).

## Deliverables

Asteroids-only mineral gym + 100-mineral seeding for existing gyms, gym-tested.

# Documentation and full project test suite validation

## Summary

Document the mineral/hold/choice mechanic in the GDD and README, add code
comments on the new modules, and validate the full project test suite.

## Acceptance Criteria

- GDD (§4.4/§4.5/§6.4 as appropriate) and README are updated to describe minerals, the hold, enemy collection/re-drop, the choice overlay and the new gym; code comments are added on new modules.
- The full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
- Test coverage for the new mineral/choice modules is reported.

## Minimal implementation

1. Update `docs/Game Design Document.md` sections §4.4/§4.5/§6.4.
2. Update `README.md` with the mechanic and the new gym.
3. Add header/behaviour comments to `Mineral.ts`, `choice.ts`, `MineralChoiceScene.ts`.
4. Run the full suite and record the result plus coverage.

## Key Files

- `docs/Game Design Document.md` (modify)
- `README.md` (modify)
- new module headers (modify)

## Dependencies

- Asteroids-only mineral gym, seeding and gym tests (final behaviour must exist before documenting).

## Deliverables

Updated GDD/README/code comments + a recorded full-suite pass and coverage report.
